host.descr: The biological species from which the neurons were derived. Use a standardized name from a taxonomy ontology like NCBITaxon (e.g., 'NCBITaxon:10090' for Mus musculus, 'Homo sapiens', 'Rattus norvegicus').

type.descr: The specific type of neuron or brain cell that was imaged. Recommended to use a term from a cell type ontology (e.g., 'pyramidal neuron', 'Purkinje cell', 'astrocyte').

region.descr: The anatomical region of the brain the sample was taken from. Recommended to use a term from a neuroanatomy atlas or ontology like ABA (e.g., 'hippocampus CA1', 'primary visual cortex', 'cerebellum').

age.descr: The date and time of the host organism's birth, used to calculate precise age at the time of experiment. Must be formatted as an ISO 8601 string (e.g., '2023-05-01T00:00:00Z').

is_ill.descr: A boolean flag indicating if the host organism had a known disease state or pathological condition at the time of sample extraction (e.g., true for a disease model, false for a wild-type control).

isolation_prot.descr: A unique identifier for the cell isolation protocol. Best practice is a DOI or permanent URL to a detailed protocol (e.g., 'dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.x54v9dd3pg1e/v1'). Alternatively, a concise lab-specific name (e.g., 'primary_dissociation_v2').

fixation_prot.descr: A unique identifier or detailed description of the chemical fixation protocol. Include fixative, concentration, duration, and temperature (e.g., '4% Paraformaldehyde in PBS for 20 minutes at room temperature').

immunohistochemistry_prot.descr: A unique identifier or detailed description of the antibody staining protocol. List primary and secondary antibodies, catalog numbers, and concentrations (e.g., 'Mouse anti-MAP2 (abcam ab1234) 1:500; Donkey anti-mouse AlexaFluor-568 (Invitrogen A10037) 1:1000').

transfection_prot.descr: The method and constructs used to introduce the fluorophore or genetic label (e.g., 'lentiviral transduction with synapsin-GFP', 'lipofectamine 3000 transfection with plasmid pEGFP-N1').

camera_pixel_size_um.descr: The physical size of a single pixel on the camera sensor, in micrometers (µm). This is a fixed property of the camera and does not account for binning or magnification.

binning.descr: The binning factor used during acquisition. For example, 2 indicates 2x2 binning, where 2x2 camera pixels are combined into one output pixel.

magnification.descr: The magnification of the objective lens used for imaging (e.g., 20, 40, 60).

physical_size_x.descr: The physical length of the entire imaged volume along the X-axis, in micrometers (µm).

physical_size_y.descr: The physical length of the entire imaged volume along the Y-axis, in micrometers (µm).

physical_size_z.descr: The physical depth or height of the entire imaged volume along the Z-axis (the stack depth), in micrometers (µm).

number_of_pixels_x.descr: The number of pixels along the X-axis of the volumetric 3D image. This defines the image width in pixels.

number_of_pixels_y.descr: The number of pixels along the Y-axis of the volumetric 3D image. This defines the image height in pixels.

number_of_pixels_z.descr: The number of slices along the Z-axis of the volumetric 3D image. This defines the image depth in pixels.

pixel_size_x.descr: The physical size of a single voxel (3D pixel) in the X dimension at the sample plane, in micrometers (µm). This is the effective pixel size after accounting for magnification and binning. Unit: µm/pixel.

pixel_size_y.descr: The physical size of a single voxel (3D pixel) in the Y dimension at the sample plane, in micrometers (µm). Often identical to pixel_size_x. Unit: µm/pixel.

pixel_size_z.descr: The physical depth of a single voxel (3D pixel) in the Z dimension (the step size), in micrometers (µm). This value is crucial for 3D reconstructions and volume calculations. Must be not negative. Unit: µm/pixel.

wavelength.descr: The central excitation wavelength(s) of the laser(s) used for each channel, in nanometers (nm). For multi-channel images, provide an array of values.

NA.descr: The Numerical Aperture of the objective lens used. This is a key determinant of resolution and light-gathering ability.
